 Daily Faceoff is a news site with no direct affiliation to the NHL, or NHLPA Golden Knights, Wild swap players in joint NHL-AHL deal
 Tyler Kuehl ( TJKu29 ) Nov 16, 2026, 21:11 EST Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Robert Edwards-Imagn Images A unique trade between a couple of Western Conference teams and their respective farm clubs.
 On Monday, the Minnesota Wild acquired defenseman Jeremy Davies from the Vegas Golden Knights for future considerations. Also, the Henderson Silver Knights, the Golden Knights’ American Hockey League affiliate, received forward Gerald Mayhew from the Wild’s primary affiliate, the Iowa Wild, for future considerations.
 The transaction is for the teams to flip-flop both players, who are both currently in the minors. However, since Davies is under an NHL contract and Mayhew is on an AHL deal, the two teams had to beat around the bush to complete the “trade.”
 Davies is in the final season of his two-year, two-way contract , which he signed in July 2025. The deal carries an NHL AAV of $1.15 million, with an AHL cap hit of $425,000. However, the 29-year-old has been with the Silver Knights for his entire tenure with the organization. So far in 2026-27, he has scored a goal and four points in 14 games. It comes after a solid 47-point performance last season, which came just shy of his career-high 48 points, which he set with the Belleville Senators during the 2024-25 campaign, the year he was named an AHL All-Star.
 It’s been a few years since Davies has been in the NHL. He was last in the big leagues during the 2022-23 campaign, when he dressed for one game with the Buffalo Sabres. In 23 games in the NHL, the Quebec native has posted three assists. In 415 regular-season games in the AHL, he has notched 54 goals and 225 points, with another 16 points in 34 Calder Cup Playoff games.
 Mayhew was in his second stint with the Iowa Wild, whom he spent the first four years of his pro career with. This year, he has scored two goals and eight points in 17 contests. The 33-year-old hasn’t had an NHL contract since the 2023-24 season, when he was a member of the Florida Panthers organization.
 The former Ferris State Bulldog has appeared in 57 NHL contests, scoring 13 goals and 15 points. In 522 regular-season appearances in the AHL, he has posted 187 goals and 360 points, with another 17 points in 26 postseason contests.
 The Silver Knights (9-5-0-0) sit tied for third in the AHL’s Pacific Division, four points back of first place. Iowa (6-9-2-1) is tied for fourth in the Central, 13 points out of first.
